title: Hardware
description: Gear up. The hardware every pentester keeps in their bag.

notices.text: Some of the tools & resources mentioned on this page require purchase.

tools.name: Arduino
tools.description: Open-source electronic prototyping platform enabling users to create interactive electronic objects.

tools.name: Raspberry Pi
tools.description: A tiny and affordable computer that you can use to learn programming through fun, practical projects.

tools.name: Attify Badge
tools.description: A hardware security assessment tool. Used to communicate between a PC and an embedded device over various hardware communication protocols.

tools.name: Goodfet
tools.description: An embedded bus adapter for various microcontrollers and radios. JTAG adapter, loosely based upon the TI MSP430 FET UIF and EZ430U boards.

tools.name: GreatFET One
tools.description: GreatFET One is a hardware hacker’s best friend. With an extensible, open source design, two USB ports, and 100 expansion pins, GreatFET One is your essential gadget for hacking, making, and reverse engineering.

tools.name: OpticSpy
tools.description: a platform to explore, evaluate, and experiment with optical data transmissions.

tools.name: Throwing Star LAN Tap/Pro
tools.description: The Great Scott Gadgets Throwing Star LAN Tap is a small, simple device for monitoring Ethernet communications.

tools.name: Pinouts
tools.description: Free book containing layouts of connectors, single board computers, dev boards, memory cards, microcontroller chips, and more.

tools.name: Hacker Warehouse
tools.description: Your one-stop shop for all your computer security needs from defense to offense.

tools.name: Hak5
tools.description: Pentest tools for authorized auditing/security analysis only where permitted.

intro: Grab some of the most used hardware within the penetration testing industry.
